title: DialEgg: Dialect-Agnostic MLIR Optimizer using Equality Saturation with Egglog
problem: Expressing compiler optimizations in MLIR is tedious; optimization interactions are complex and unpredictable, making it difficult to achieve full performance potential. Equality saturation could solve this but remains absent from production compilers like MLIR.
motivation: Integrating equality saturation (which systematically explores all optimization interactions through saturation) with MLIR enables more expressive, composable optimizations while reducing manual rewrite-rule engineering.
method: DialEgg connects Egglog (an equality saturation engine—a tool that systematically generates and tests all mathematically equivalent forms of code to find the fastest version) to MLIR, a compiler optimization framework used across many programming languages. Rather than writing separate optimization rules for each MLIR variant (dialect), DialEgg automatically translates code back and forth between MLIR and Egglog formats. It comes with pre-built definitions for common MLIR operations, types, and attributes, so developers can benefit from equality saturation immediately.
key_novelty: DialEgg applies equality saturation (systematically finding all mathematically equivalent forms of code and choosing the fastest) to MLIR without needing separate implementations for each compiler dialect.
contributions: A dialect-agnostic framework (DialEgg) for integrating Egglog equality saturation with MLIR
Modeling of MLIR constructs (operations, types, attributes) in Egglog representation
Automatic translation between MLIR and Egglog program representations with pre-defined common constructs

metrics.other: potential for combining equality saturation and MLIR demonstrated

limitations: Use-case evaluation is preliminary; quantitative performance gains not detailed in abstract.
primary_theme: Dialect-agnostic equality saturation integration for MLIR
